boundaries: Open-first reader validates actual fstat bigint file identity, regular-file type, link count1 and per-input limit before allocation.
Reads use explicit offsets and at most64KiB per call, stop at initial fstat size and probe exact EOF; post-read fstat catches growth, truncation, metadata or inode changes.
Observed file path and every ancestor are rechecked; source capture additionally compares original bigint/nanosecond stamps.
Both saved handles and all three descriptor/receipt/executable handles stay open through validation and final observed-path checks.

Exclusive recreated fixture write cannot overwrite an existing path; underlying saved byte and rename/recreate refusal assertions are retained.
Producer non-recursive owned-stage cleanup and ancestor ownership checks remain; foreign content is preserved on refusal.
limitations: Path observations are separate syscalls, not atomic namespace locking on Windows or other platforms. Final producer handles close before seal rename, matching the existing observed-path threat boundary.
